humanities_role_explanation: Items are museum heritage objects and the task is cataloguing-style inference of culture, period, origin and creator from images, i.e. a disciplinary (art-historical/museological) competence rather than generic ability.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Image-only input of heritage objects; models output text/JSON structured metadata, which is judged by an LLM against textual museum metadata.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Structured metadata inference (culture, period, origin, creator, title) from images of ceramics, paintings, metalwork and sculpture; the paper calls these 'non-observable cultural attributes'. Captions are generated and mapped to structured fields; attribution of period, origin and creator is central.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to a single task: image-to-structured cultural metadata inference for heritage objects.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Nine VLMs: Qwen-VL-Max, Qwen3-VL-Plus/Flash/8B/32B, Pixtral-12B, GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-5.4-mini, Claude Haiku 4.5; GPT-4.1-mini as judge.

quantitative_metrics.note: Exact-match accuracy, partial-match rate, attribute-level accuracy via LLM-as-Judge.

summary: Appear2Meaning is a cross-cultural benchmark of 750 Getty and Met heritage objects across four regions and four object types, testing whether VLMs can infer structured metadata (culture, period, origin, creator, title) from images alone. Nine VLMs are scored by an LLM judge; exact-match is very low while partial match is higher, with notable variation across regions.
key_findings: Exact match accuracy is 0.005-0.029; partial match up to 0.658 (Qwen3-VL-Flash). Title and creator are easier than culture, period, origin. East Asia performs best and Europe/Americas worst; errors include Eurocentric misattribution, period compression and creator memorisation.
facets_explanation: Ground truth is structured metadata taken from Getty and Met open-access records; human annotators only selected objects and verified region/type assignment. Answers require knowledge not visible in the image (period, origin, creator). Scoring is by a GPT-4.1-mini judge labelling correct/partial/incorrect on semantic alignment. The paper discusses the limits of single-reference metadata but does not treat annotator disagreement.
results_explanation: Table 3: Qwen3-VL-Flash has the highest partial match 0.658 (converted to 65.8 points); the best exact-match accuracy is 0.029 (Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct). The gap of 65 points is Qwen3-VL-Flash partial 0.658 versus exact 0.014, rounded down from 64.4 to 65 only approximately; the largest is about 0.644 for that model. Per-region results show East Asia strongest ('highest partial match rates observed for Qwen3-VL-Flash (0.740)') and Americas/Europe lower. No human baseline reported.

humanities_role.quote: By requiring models to predict structured museum metadata from image-only input, this task asks whether VLMs can infer non-observable cultural attributes beyond perceptual features

dataset_size.quote: We sample 50 artifacts per culture–type combination, resulting in 750 objects.

evaluation_set_size.quote: Only verified objects are retained, resulting in 750 validated samples.

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: All models are evaluated on the benchmark described in Section 3.1 under an image-only setting.

gold_source.quote: Each object includes the original image and structured metadata from museum databases, used as ground truth in Section 3.1.

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: these attributes are typically not directly observable from visual features alone and require cultural and historical knowledge

answer_multiplicity.quote: GPT-4.1-mini compares predictions with reference metadata and assigns labels (correct, partially correct, incorrect).

reported_format_gap_kind.quote: partial match rates are substantially higher, suggesting that models often capture some correct attributes but fail to produce fully consistent predictions

reported_best_score.quote: Qwen3-VL-Flash achieves the highest partial match rate (0.658)

reported_cultural_asymmetry.quote: East Asia consistently yields the strongest performance across models
